title: Introduce per-tenant adaptive batching windows and lightweight KV warmup shim
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: The continuous batching layer currently uses a global heuristic for batch window sizing which leads to suboptimal batching for multi-tenant traffic. Low QPS tenants see long artificial batching delays to meet batch targets, and high QPS tenants occasionally generate oversized batches that increase tail latency and memory pressure. Separately, KV cache warmup for model swaps and slot allocation remains ad hoc and causes transient KV miss storms after scale events, harming p95 latency and increasing token costs.

Proposal: Implement a per-tenant adaptive batching window combined with a lightweight KV warmup shim that primes hot prefixes for tenants when slots are allocated or model variants are swapped. Key components: 1) Tenant-level batching policies that track short-term QPS, latency SLOs, and historical batch size distributions to dynamically tighten or relax the batching window. 2) A shim that runs as a best-effort prefetcher when a slot is assigned or a model swap occurs; it queries the KV index for top-N hot prefixes for the tenant and asynchronously populates the local KV cache before traffic ramps. 3) Scheduler cleanup to extract the tenant policy evaluation out of the hot path into a small control loop and add an explicit preemption signal for oversized batches. 4) Observability: per-tenant histograms for batch size, batching delay, KV miss ratio, and a new rollout dashboard for the canary.

Benefits: Reduced p95 token latency for mixed-tenant workloads, faster stabilization after scale/model events, and lower KV backend egress from fewer cold misses. The design aims to limit code churn in the core batch commit path by routing tenant policy decisions through a non-blocking control plane thread.

Trade-offs and risks: The per-tenant policy increases memory for metadata and introduces tuning knobs (window bounds, warmup budget). Warmup can increase short-term KV reads which may show up as increased cost if misconfigured. There's a risk of stale policy estimates for very bursty tenants; mitigations include conservative rate limits and fallback to global windowing.
acceptance_criteria: Deployable behind runtime feature flag toggles for per-tenant batching and KV warmup
Canary run for 48 hours on low-risk region with automated rollback if p95 token latency increases by >5% or KV miss rate increases by >10%
Observed decrease in KV miss ratio by at least 8% and p95 token latency improvement of at least 5% on mixed-tenant synthetic workload compared to baseline
No increase in out-of-memory incidents attributed to batching or warmup during the canary period
Unit and integration tests covering policy edge cases, warmup failures, and control-plane separation
tasks: Design: finalize per-tenant policy state machine and storage layout (Aisha)
Implement: tenant policy evaluator and control loop (Liam)
Implement: KV warmup shim and async prefetch worker (Eng-2)
Scheduler: add explicit preemption signal and move policy checks off hot path (Eng-3)
Observability: add per-tenant histograms and rollout dashboard (SRE)
E2E: synthetic workload test harness for mixed-tenant scenarios (QA)

Docs: design doc, operator runbook, and runtime config reference page (DX)
Postmortem: short review after canary to capture adjustments and tuning
comments: 2026-02-18 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after postmortem of a KV miss storm during a model swap in us-west-2. Initial measurement: p95 token latency regressed ~12% for mixed small/large tenants during the incident.

2026-02-22 Liam Brooks: Spike complete. Confirmed that tenant-local moving average of QPS plus CDF of batch sizes can be used to derive a safe window bound. Memory overhead estimated at ~140 bytes per active tenant, acceptable for current scale.
2026-02-27 SRE: Prototype warmup increased short-term KV reads by 22% but reduced misses by 35% in lab. Need throttling to avoid backend pressure on large rollouts.
2026-03-03 PM (Jon Tsai): Prioritize observability and rollout gates. Add automated rollback if costs exceed threshold during canary.
2026-03-05 Design review: Opted for a conservative default policy (min-window 2ms, max-window 30ms) and tenant-level weight-based warmup budget. Design doc linked below.
2026-03-08 Liam Brooks: Started implementation of control loop. Pushed initial branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1842
2026-03-10 QA: Synthetic harness ready. Running baseline vs feature flag comparisons on staging cluster. Initial pass shows p95 improvement ~6% and KV miss reduction ~11% for mixed workload.
2026-03-10 Decision: Break into two rolling features - (A) per-tenant batching control and (B) KV warmup shim. Rollout batching first with warmup gated until warmup throttles are implemented.
engineering_notes: Keep hot path changes minimal: control loop writes compact policy snapshots to an epoched ring buffer that workers read lock-free
Warmup shim should prefer async best-effort prefetch and never block slot allocation; provide backpressure token that rejects warmup when KV backend QPS > threshold
Add feature flags with rollout percentage and per-tenant opt-out for enterprise customers during canary
Consider a future enhancement: tenant-level learned models to predict hot prefixes based on recent prompt prefixes
Benchmark targets: end-to-end p95 token latency down 5-8% on mixed workload, KV backend read volume neutral or down after stabilization
